reader.requirement: At --std 85 every record of a relative file is identified by its relative record number, its logical ordinal position: the first record is 1 and later records 2, 3, 4, ...; sequential release from OPEN OUTPUT starts at 1 and ascends consecutively, EXTEND continues from highest+1, random/dynamic access stores and finds a record at the number in the relative key, and sequential retrieval delivers existing records in ascending number order (§1985:VIII.2.4.4 GR2), returning each one's number in the relative key.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.RelativeWriteKeyOutOfRangeIsPermanentError: a random/dynamic WRITE whose key is < 1 or above HighestRelativeRecordNumber answers '24' (invalid key, write beyond the externally defined boundaries, §1985:VIII.1.3.4) below 2014 and '34' (permanent error) from 2014

reader.edition-search: read RelativeConnector Write/Read/Start/Opened/NextSequentialSlot; grep DialectBehavior/Edition in RelativeConnector.cs; the selection rules (SelectSequentialSlot) take no edition parameter, numbering is edition-invariant.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only for an out-of-range key on a random WRITE (85 '24' invalid key, 2014+ '34' permanent error); the numbering itself (first record 1, then 2, 3, ...) is the same at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c24_relative_record_numbering covers the ordinal numbering; key 0 on WRITE/READ/START, EXTEND continuation, a sparse file, variable-length records and the key-size boundary are exercised by this slice's probes

probes.printed: SEQWRITE SK=0001/0002/0003 (OPEN OUTPUT, RECORD VARYING 1 TO 10 DEPENDING ON); W7 ST=00; W0 INV 24; R0 INV 23; S0 INV 23; NEXT DK=0001 LEN=01 A, 0002 LEN=02 AB, 0003 LEN=03 ABC, 0007 LEN=02 XY, EOF 10; EXTWRITE SK=0008; SEQ SK=0001,0002,0003,0007,0008, EOF 10
probes.expected: first record 1, then 2, 3; record 7 stored at ordinal 7; sequential access in ascending order of existing records; EXTEND gives highest+1; key 0 names no record (WRITE invalid key 24 per §1985:VIII.1.3.4 (3) c, READ/START 23)

probes.printed: W10 INV 24 SK=9 (RELATIVE KEY PIC 9, tenth sequential WRITE); WBIG INV 24 (key 999999999999999999); WMAX ST=00; RMAX ST=00 MAX (key 2147483647)
probes.expected: tenth record's number 10 has more digits than the key item: invalid key 24 (§1985:VIII.1.3.4 (3) c); a key beyond the implementor's boundary is 24; the implementor's highest number is stored and read back

reader.notes: Sequential release takes max(highest existing, last released)+1, so OPEN OUTPUT numbers from 1 consecutively and EXTEND from highest+1; random access stores at the key's ordinal; sequential selection is one ascending seek over existing records. The only edition arm is the out-of-range WRITE status, and the 85 arm ('24') matches the 1985 I-O status list.
